# Commands

<!-- Generated by pnpm run docs:generate. Edit the implementation, then regenerate both audiences. -->

These are the commands the doodlebot plugin adds. In Claude Code, type the command followed by its arguments; in Codex, choose the skill of the same name from the skill picker. See [Install the plugin](../get-started/install.md). This page is generated from each command's skill file.

## Set up and run the test Vortex

Install, check, sign in and update the companion, and prepare the Vortex source.

| Command             | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Arguments                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `/doodlebot:setup`  | Install, repair, check, sign in or update doodlebot on this machine (modes: setup, --check, --login, --update [&lt;ref>]); use once per machine, to see what this machine can test, or when another command says doodlebot is not set up.                                                            | <code>[--check &#124; --login [--dev-dir &lt;checkout&gt;] &#124; --update [&lt;ref&gt;]] [folder] [--ref &lt;tag or branch&gt;] [--bin-dir &lt;folder&gt;]</code> |
| `/doodlebot:source` | Prepare the Vortex checkout this session is opened in (remotes and exclude after your yes, install and build), clone a new one into a folder you name, cut a work branch from upstream, or check out a pull request's branch for QA; use before changing, investigating or QA-ing Vortex's own code. | <code>[--clone &lt;dir&gt; &#124; --branch &lt;name&gt; &#124; --pr &lt;number&gt;] [--update]</code>                                                              |

## Work on Vortex

Try things in a test Vortex, investigate and fix bugs, QA changes and releases, and ship pull requests.

| Command                  | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Arguments                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/doodlebot:try`         | Try something in a test Vortex (look, click, install, deploy, a collection) on a release, the installed Vortex or a source build, choosing the content itself, and return a run report; use for 'does X work?' or to see a change working.                                                                              | <code>&lt;what to do in Vortex&gt; [on &lt;release version &#124; installed &#124; my build&gt;] [with &lt;content&gt;] [fresh]</code>   |
| `/doodlebot:investigate` | Find out why something in Vortex is broken, from a description, an issue link or a user's vortex.log: reproduce it on the user's version and narrow it to the cause in the source, returning an issue report; changes no code. Use for 'why is this broken?'.                                                           | <code>&lt;description, issue link or path to a user's vortex.log&gt;</code>                                                              |
| `/doodlebot:fix`         | Fix a Vortex bug end to end: from an issue report (or investigating first), branch, fix, add the regression test to the Vortex branch, prove it with a revert control and the reproduction on the fix, then offer the PR; use for 'fix it'.                                                                             | <code>&lt;issue report path, bug report, issue link or symptom&gt;</code>                                                                |
| `/doodlebot:qa`          | QA a Vortex change from a fresh profile: a branch or PR (base build, then PR build), a design's acceptance criteria with negative controls, or a new release or nightly against the previous one; returns a QA report and posts to a PR only when you say so. Use for 'review / QA this PR' or 'check the new release'. | <code>&lt;PR number or URL &#124; branch&gt; &#124; --design &lt;file&gt; &#124; --release &lt;version&gt; [entry ids to include]</code> |
| `/doodlebot:pr`          | Ship a verified Vortex change as a pull request: preflight with the revert check, build pr/&lt;topic> without the design commits, write the description with the design summary and the doodlebot footer, push only to your fork, and read CI when it is red; use for 'ship it' after a fix or feature.                 | <code>&lt;topic&gt; [checkout] [PR number, once it exists] [ready]</code>                                                                |

## Benchmark

Measure a Vortex build, or compare two.

| Command              | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Arguments                                                                                |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/doodlebot:measure` | Measure a Vortex build on one of doodlebot's performance checks, run several times, and report medians and ranges; with a second build, run both alternately and give a rule-based verdict. Use for 'is it faster?' or 'did this make X slower?'. | <code>--a &lt;build&gt; [--b &lt;build&gt;] --check &lt;check&gt; [check options]</code> |
